head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
changes: Registered evaluation views borrow input/public values, zero rows, repeated challenge patterns and terminal values instead of materializing duplicate arrays.

A scoped compiler scratch helper admits exact backing capacity against the shared construction quota before allocation. It releases storage and reservation on success, error and unwind without discarding the peak.
Periodic/permutation evaluation results and the ordered constraint table use that shared scratch quota; caller-provided slices cannot grow or escape the scoped allocation.
Quotient vanishing values use fixed scratch for the supported 32-chunk maximum. Constraint emission checks reject duplicate, missing and out-of-range indexes.

Frozen lowering/PCS references, real uni/wallet/batch tampering tests and original full-size registry verification pass. Proof formats, parameters, activation and assigned worker limits remain unchanged.
limitations: Construction counters describe requested builder-owned storage, not physical RSS. Caller-owned proof data, public constant/periodic source buffers, remaining compiler/symbolic scratch, cached programs and driver/allocator overhead still need complete enclosing lifetime reservations.

The construction requirement is for the recorded compiler path. A different construction path may require a larger allowance even when it produces an equal program; the quota still rejects excess growth.

The complete scheduler lifetime profile remains unfinished. Ordinary fleet planning rejects this qualification profile without phases; adaptive GPU phases must reserve their enforced aggregate cap unless runtime tile constraints are introduced.
No scheduler allowance has been reduced from observed memory peaks. The same 3 GiB worker, 4 GiB aggregate host, 7 GiB managed GPU and 1 GiB allocation caps remain enforced.
Both finalizers prove the same terminal statement through distinct verified dependencies. Their timings do not establish sustained transactions per hour.
Other transaction types, nonempty-child full-size merges, larger blocks, sustained pool throughput, multi-GPU saturation and AMD/Metal qualification remain open.
